subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should urgent `system event` delivery be an operator-visible alert surface, a prompt-visible transcript injection path, or both with separate ordering contracts?
rationale: Current code intentionally defers heartbeat when a same-session turn is active, while queued system events later become trusted `System:` prompt content; bypassing that guard changes both product semantics and a security boundary.

options.title: Split alert and transcript paths
options.body: Add a typed urgent operator alert path for immediate TUI/control visibility and keep prompt-visible system events ordered through a separately reviewed queue/drain contract.

options.title: Allow prompt-visible priority injection
options.body: Add an explicit high-priority prompt/transcript event mode with strict authorization, ordering, and regression tests for active turns.

options.title: Defer to scheduler fairness
options.body: Keep `system event` best-effort for now and solve foreground/background ordering through the broader session-lane policy tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/54488.

recommendation.title: Split alert and transcript paths
recommendation.body: Add a typed urgent operator alert path for immediate TUI/control visibility and keep prompt-visible system events ordered through a separately reviewed queue/drain contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent landed wake/session-key changes and current-source blame point to steipete as the best available owner for the security/product boundary decision.
